statusText: CME equity-index futures have been shut since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and do not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, so there is no observable NQ price path this hour and none anywhere in the 24-hour horizon, which ends at 06:00 UTC on 16 August - still about 16 hours before the reopen. Tail holds at 10% (low), keeping the action at EA_ON and the status green: pathological one-way structure cannot form while no venue is quoting, and the low non-zero level prices weekend headline discontinuity rather than any observed extension. This hour added no new escalation - the newest entry on the live wire remains Treasury Secretary Bessent's 06:05 UTC threat of economic isolation 'like the world has never seen before' with measures due next week, which the previous run already scored - so nothing in the risk set moved. The last confirmed structure, re-verified this hour from primary sources, is unchanged: September E-mini NQ settled at 30,148.25 (last print 30,141.75, -46.75 or -0.15% against a 30,188.50 previous close), mid-range inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 band, while the Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14 (-0.13%) in a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range and about 2.3% below its 52-week high of 30,762.20, with VIX at 14.25 (-2.60%, day range 14.18-14.72) and H.15 showing 2Y 4.15%, 10Y 4.63% and 30Y 5.21% for 13 August. Stress holds at 48% (elevated) because the escalation set neither widened nor resolved in the last hour: the strait is still blocked pending Iran's conditions, the U.S. naval blockade is still in force, the UAE still blames Iran for Thursday's drone attacks on two ADNOC tankers, the Ansar strike in southern Lebanon that killed seven remains the deadliest since the 26 June framework, WTI sits at $82.40 (+1.42% on the day, more than +5% on the week) and Brent near $88.5, and Friday's U.S. consumer data was sharply soft with Retail Sales -0.6% against +0.1% expected and Michigan sentiment 51.0 against 54.5. Confidence is 59% (medium-low): everything except the price path is fresh and primary-sourced, but the price path is the input that matters most and it does not exist this hour. The operative checkpoint remains the Sunday CME reopen, which the danger window brackets.
recommendation: Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail (10%) alone. No venue is quoting NQ anywhere in the 24-hour horizon and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside it, so there is no basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window; existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The operative checkpoint is the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, where a full weekend of accumulated headlines would express as an opening gap rather than as intraday structure - the danger window brackets that reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery. Gap risk is genuinely two-way: escalation from the Ansar strike, the ADNOC tanker attacks, an indefinite blockade posture and a reported 17 August sanctions deadline pull one way, while the unsigned but reportedly close Iran-Oman routing arrangement and Tehran's stated willingness to reopen on terms pull the other. Crude can move before equities are able to price it, and Friday's weak consumer prints leave a second, unrelated growth-scare channel open into the 19 August FOMC minutes. This is a general market-risk assessment for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and no trade is being placed or recommended.
headline: Third straight hour with no tape and no new escalation: CME stays shut until Sunday, the Hormuz blockade and the Ansar strike remain unresolved rather than worsened, and Tail holds at 10% on EA_ON with Stress steady at 48%.
body:
PRICE PATH (observed, stale by necessity). No venue has quoted NQ since the CME weekly close at 21:00 UTC on Friday 14 August, and none will until the Sunday reopen near 22:00 UTC on 16 August. The last live structure, re-verified this hour from primary sources, remains benign: September E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures show a last print of 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15% against a previous close of 30,188.50, with the session settling mid-range inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 band roughly 255 points or 0.84% wide, and no close near either extreme. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14, -38.36 points or -0.13%, inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range, about 2.3% below the 52-week high of 30,762.20 and well above the 22,841.42 low. A two-way intraday range with a mid-range settle is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks and repeated extension that the Tail definition requires. Directional efficiency, pullback depth, failed-retracement counts and proximity to session extremes are all unobservable this hour; that is a structural absence of evidence, not evidence of calm, and it is the single reason Confidence stays medium-low.

CROSS-ASSET (observed, Friday close). VIX closed at 14.25, -0.38 or -2.60%, in a 14.18-14.72 day range and near the bottom of its 13.38-35.30 52-week band - the options market priced no stress into the weekend. The latest H.15 constant-maturity yields, for 13 August, are 2Y 4.15%, 10Y 4.63% and 30Y 5.21%: a positively sloped curve with no acute front-end repricing, and no update is due before Monday. Crude is the one asset carrying the geopolitical premium, and it is carrying it clearly - WTI $82.40, +$1.15 or +1.42% on the day and more than +5% on the week, +3.52% on the month and roughly +33% year-over-year; Brent settled near $88.5 after a comparable weekly gain. This is a textbook conflicting-signal set: equity volatility asleep, rates orderly, energy repricing a supply shock. Per the risk definitions, conflicting signals belong in Stress, not Tail, and that is exactly where they are scored.

GEOPOLITICS (no new escalation this hour). The distinguishing feature of this run is what did not happen. A fresh sweep of the live wires produced nothing that postdates the previous assessment: the newest timestamped entry is still Treasury Secretary Bessent at 06:05 UTC threatening Iran with economic isolation 'like the world has never seen before', with new measures expected next week and a dual approach combining financial pressure with a physical blockade of Iranian ports. The overnight developments already scored remain the live ones - the Israeli airstrike on a home at Ansar in southern Lebanon that killed seven and wounded three, the deadliest toll since the 26 June framework arrangements, and the UAE's accusation that Iran was behind Thursday evening's drone attacks on two ADNOC-linked tankers transiting Hormuz. The standing impasse is intact: the Persian Gulf Strait Authority maintains the strait 'remains blocked and will not be reopened until Iran's conditions are accepted', chiefly sanctions relief and the release of frozen assets; Iran's national security chief Mohsen Rezaie adds an end to Israel's wars in Lebanon and Gaza to those conditions; the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports remains in force with vessels still being redirected; Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi answered Trump's claim on the waterway by saying at 01:44 UTC that it 'cannot be seized by tweet, nor by aircraft carrier'; and the Iran-Oman routing arrangement remains unsigned. Shipping traffic through the strait is still running far below the roughly 120 large vessels a day seen before the war. An unresolved escalation that stops widening for one hour is not an improving one - it is the same live transmission channel into crude waiting for a venue to price it, which is why Stress holds rather than decays.

MACRO (observed). Friday's U.S. consumer prints both missed sharply: Retail Sales -0.6% month-over-month against +0.1% consensus, Retail Sales ex-autos -0.3% against +0.2%, and preliminary August Michigan sentiment 51.0 against 54.5 consensus. Equities absorbed those misses on Friday with two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency - the reason Tail sat at 7-9% through the cash session while Stress built into the low 40s. The soft-consumer channel is a second, independent thread into the 19 August FOMC minutes, unrelated to the Middle East. No U.S. macro release falls inside this 24-hour horizon; the calendar restarts with the NY Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC on Monday 17 August.

SCORING (inference). Tail 10% - low band, EA_ON, green. A shut venue cannot produce a pathological price path, and none of the amplifier conditions the contract requires for 25%+ is observable, let alone confirmed. The level is unchanged from the previous hour because the input that moved it - new escalation - did not repeat. Stress 48% - elevated, unchanged, because the escalation set neither widened nor resolved, and because a shut market defers rather than removes the repricing; letting Stress decay toward trivial levels while the strait is blocked and a sanctions deadline sits two days out would misstate the backdrop. Confidence 59% - medium-low. Every obtainable input was obtained and re-verified against primary sources this hour; the gap is structural, and a weekend futures halt with no live price path is precisely the case the contract reserves the medium-low band for. Dominant mode is mixed: a halted tape overlaid on genuinely conflicting cross-asset signals and two-way geopolitical threads.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 2-10% throughout. It held 9% through Friday's European session, eased to 7-9% across the U.S. cash session as the sharp Retail Sales and Michigan sentiment misses produced two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency, and printed 6% into the 21:00 UTC weekly close. Stress described a clear event arc: 25-28% in the quiet Friday morning hours, building to 40-44% through the U.S. cash session as the data landed, then 34% at the close. The two runs immediately after the close scored the halt itself at Tail 2% and Stress 12%; from 00:00 UTC onward that reading was corrected back to Tail 9% and Stress 45% on the judgement that a shut venue does not neutralise a live Hormuz closure, and 45% then held for six consecutive hours through 05:00 UTC. The 06:00 UTC slot lifted to Tail 10% and Stress 48% on genuinely new overnight escalation - the Ansar strike in southern Lebanon and the UAE's accusation over the ADNOC tanker attacks - and this hour holds both levels because nothing further printed. Those past opinions are preserved exactly as published and have not been rewritten. Confidence spent the Friday session in the 30s-50s and firmed to 56-59% after midnight as primary-source verification improved. One slot, 20:00 UTC on 14 August, has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it runs from 07:00 UTC on Saturday 15 August to 06:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, ending roughly 16 hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day - so neither a scheduled U.S. macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is therefore projected flat at 10% for the first thirteen slots and ticking to 11% from 20:00 UTC on 15 August as the reopen edges into view; that increment reflects accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays deep in the low band, so the action is EA_ON and the status green throughout. Stress is projected to ease at most a point to 47% through the thin Saturday European and U.S. afternoon hours, when weekend headline flow is historically lightest, then firm back to 48-49% into the late slots as unresolved threads converge on Sunday's price discovery: the Hormuz impasse and Tehran's insistence on sanctions relief, asset unfreezing and an end to the Lebanon and Gaza wars, the indefinite-blockade posture and the reported 17 August deadline for unprecedented new curbs, the fresh Lebanon escalation and its bearing on the June framework, the unsigned Iran-Oman routing arrangement, and a soft U.S. consumer picture heading into the 19 August FOMC minutes. Confidence stays in the medium-low band at 58-59% for as long as no venue quotes. The real checkpoint sits just beyond this horizon: the reopen at roughly 22:00 UTC on 16 August, which the danger window brackets together with its first 90 minutes of trade. Gap risk there is two-way, and the first live tape - not this forecast - is what will decide whether Tail leaves the low band.

forecastDetail.comment: Current hour, European Saturday morning and the third full day of the CME weekend halt. No venue quotes NQ, so directional efficiency, pullback depth, repeated extension and proximity to session extremes are all unobservable; Tail 10% prices weekend headline discontinuity alone, not observed structure. The level is flat on the hour because the wires produced nothing new - the most recent timestamped item is still Bessent's 06:05 UTC sanctions threat, already scored.

European mid-morning. Still no tradable tape anywhere. Stress holds at 48% because the escalation set neither widened nor resolved: the strait stays blocked pending Iran's conditions, the U.S. naval blockade stays in force, the UAE still blames Iran for Thursday's drone attacks on two ADNOC tankers, and Tehran continues to insist the waterway opens only under its own command.

European midday. Stress eases one point to 47% on the historical pattern of a quiet Saturday news cycle, not on any resolution; nothing in the underlying set has changed. The two live threads - the Hormuz impasse and the Lebanon strikes - remain capable of producing a wire story at any hour, but none of it can express as a price path until Sunday's reopen.

Early U.S. Saturday. Confidence stays medium-low at 59% - every non-price input was re-verified against primary sources this hour and is current, but the price path, the input that matters most, does not exist. That is a structural absence of evidence rather than evidence of calm, and it is the sole reason the band is not higher.

U.S. Saturday late morning. No scheduled U.S. macro release falls anywhere in this 24-hour horizon; the next is the NY Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC on Monday 17 August. The absence of a data catalyst is why Stress rests on the geopolitical and crude backdrop alone rather than on event dispersion.

U.S. Saturday midday. Roughly 34 hours remain to the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday. Tail holds at 10% and the status stays green; the accumulating gap risk is real but is still more than a day away and is genuinely two-way, with a reported 17 August U.S. sanctions deadline and the unsigned Iran-Oman routing arrangement pulling in opposite directions.
